chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah said:

I asked him about the patient who loses consciousness. He said: 'If three days pass over him, there is no qada (make-up) upon him; and if he is unconscious for three days, then upon him is the qada of the prayer during those days.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up missed prayers for a patient who is unconscious for three days?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction regarding *qada* (make-up) prayers for a patient experiencing prolonged unconsciousness (*ghafla*). It establishes that if the state of unconsciousness persists continuously for three days without any interval of lucidity, the obligation of prayer is lifted; conversely, if the person regains consciousness even briefly within that period, they remain liable for the missed prayers. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the preservation of religious duty while accommodating genuine physical incapacity.
